description: Record what a node relates to — or that nothing does. Use it right after capturing an idea, decision or requirement, while the search you ran to check for duplicates is still in hand: those near-matches are the candidates, and today they are read once and thrown away. Draw the relations that are genuinely true (`CONTRADICTS`, `EVOLVES_INTO`, `DEPENDS_ON`, `CAUSES`, `TRIGGERS`, `BLOCKS`, `DUPLICATES`, `ANTICIPATES`, `OBSOLETES`, `RISKS`, `MITIGATES`, `MASKS`, `VIOLATES`), each with the reason in `evidence`. ⚠️ A CONTRADICTS is stored `alignment: opposing` — a conflict, which `detect_defects` reports — unless the link says `"alignment": "supporting"`: that field, not the evidence, is how a link records corroboration. A link overrides the other defaults the same way: CAUSES `basis` (stored `correlational` when unsaid) and `validation_status` (`unvalidated`), DUPLICATES `basis` (`suspected`), DEPENDS_ON `optional` (`false`) and `weight_basis` (`estimated`); one its relation does not declare is refused. Two or three is a good outcome; ten is a smell, because relatedness is not similarity. If nothing is honestly related, pass `note` instead — that is a real answer, not a weaker one, and it is what tells a later reader this node was considered rather than never opened. NEVER invent a relation to have something to pass: a false neighbour is worse than a missing one, since anything that searches by neighbourhood repeats it forever. Refuses when you give neither.

alignment.description:
CONTRADICTS only. `opposing`: the two conflict — and what an unsaid
alignment is STORED AS, which `detect_defects` reports as a
contradiction. `supporting`: they corroborate each other. `conceding`:
a reply grants an objection against what it attacks (draw it with
create_edge to name the reading it moves to, `moves_to`). Saying
"corroboration" in `evidence` does not set it; only this field does.

basis.description:
CAUSES: how strongly the link is grounded — `observed`,
`correlational` (stored when unsaid: a co-variation, not a cause),
`causal` (only with a mechanism) or `spurious`. DUPLICATES: who
decided the two cover the same ground — `asserted` (a person says so)
or `suspected` (stored when unsaid; never merged).

evidence.description:
WHY this relation is true, in a sentence. Required — a relation with no
evidence is an assertion the next reader can neither check nor overturn.

incoming.description:
Draw the edge FROM the other node instead. Direction is part of the
claim: every one of these reads as a sentence, *from RELATION to*, and
backwards the same edge asserts something false with nothing to catch it.

optional.description:
DEPENDS_ON only: `true` when the source works without the target.
Unsaid, the dependency is stored as required (`false`).

other_design.description:
When the other node lives in ANOTHER DESIGN: that design's id. `other_id`
is then the node's id THERE, and this design keeps a reference standing
in for it (`xref:<design>:<node>`), so the link is typed and checkable:
`upstream_status` reports a link into a design this one does not declare,
and one whose far design has changed since the link was made. Linking
again acknowledges it.

other_id.description:
The node at the other end of the relation (`req:…`, `dec:…`, any node id).
The edge runs TO it unless `incoming` turns it round. Its type is resolved
from the id; `other_type` names it when the id is ambiguous.

other_name.description:
With `other_design`: the far node's name as you read it there, so the
reference reads as more than an id.

other_type.description:
Optional since 2026-09-06: resolved from the id when omitted (the id
prefix names the type); an id held by more than one type is REFUSED, never
guessed — pass it then.

relation.description:
`CONTRADICTS` (both cannot hold) / `EVOLVES_INTO` (the older thought,
grown up) / `DEPENDS_ON` (only worth anything if the other lands first)
/ `CAUSES` / `TRIGGERS` (taking one forces the other) / `BLOCKS` /
`DUPLICATES` (the same thing said twice — link, do not merge; they were
said for different reasons) / `ANTICIPATES` (the earlier one saw this
coming) / `OBSOLETES` / `RISKS` / `MITIGATES` (one is a hazard, the
other answers it) / `MASKS` / `VIOLATES`.

validation_status.description:
CAUSES only: how far the claim has been tested — `unvalidated` (stored
when unsaid), `hypothesis`, `validated` or `refuted`.

weight_basis.description:
DEPENDS_ON only: how the coupling weight was set — `estimated` (stored
when unsaid), `evidence` or `measured`.

echo.description: What the reply carries. `receipt` (the default) names the node, echoes each stored value of at most 200 characters, gives longer ones by size, and names the snapshot that keeps anything a revise replaced. `node` returns the whole stored node and every prior value.

links.description:
The relations you judged to be real. Empty is a valid answer — pass
`note` instead.

node_id.description: The reviewed node; its type is `node_type`.

node_type.description:
The node whose relations were reviewed (e.g. `Decision`).
Optional since 2026-09-06: resolved from the id when omitted (the id
prefix names the type); an id held by more than one type is REFUSED, never
guessed — pass it then.

note.description:
Required when `links` is empty: what you searched, what was nearest, and
why nothing was honestly related. This is the half people skip, and it
is what separates a node somebody judged and found genuinely new from
one nobody has opened — without it the two are the same node.

name: review_relations
title: Review a Node's Relations
